links.outcome: Readability of GPT-4 patient education responses (Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
links.effect: Flesch Reading Ease 50.13; Gunning Fog 12.68, corresponding to a 12th-grade reading level, above the recommended sixth to eighth grade.
links.quote: Readability analyses indicated moderate complexity (Flesch Reading Ease Score: 50.13; Gunning Fog Index: 12.68), corresponding to a 12th-grade reading level.

links.outcome: Rate of hallucinated and real references in GPT-4 responses
links.effect: 11.8% (383/3250) of references hallucinated; 88.2% (2867/3250) real, with 95.1% (2724/2867) from authoritative sources.
links.quote: Reference Evaluation for Artificial Intelligence identified 11.8% (383/3250) hallucinated references, while 88.2% (2867/3250) of references were real, with 95.1% (2724/2867) from authoritative sources (eg, government guidelines and the literature).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates GPT-4's performance (accuracy, safety, readability, and reference hallucinations) on patient education questions regarding scars and keloids using expert clinician evaluation, but it does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
